text: What #790's review found past its plan, fixed by hand before #799 merged. Its independent review reproduced a saved proposal whose module name climbed out of its project: ratification wrote an include five directories up and removed the model file planted there. Every fingerprint can be recomputed to match such a name, so a digest that matches says nothing about it. Any proposal about to be ratified, read from its comment or from a saved record, now meets the rules an issue's own Project line meets: a clean directory inside the repository, outside .git, .github, .invariant and decisions in any spelling, with no backslash, control character or name that starts with a dash; a CamelCase module name; for an amendment, a .tla module path inside its project; and a slug that is one plain name, kebab case for a new project. Proposal.Write refuses the same, and one that isn't leaves its ratification pending. A marker of the factory's own, known by its App's login, that no longer reads anywhere in its JSON, gzip or base64 now stops the issue, as a broken reference does, where a cut before the reference's key let the earlier proposal answer; a person restores the comment or deletes it to fall back on purpose, and with no App a marker that doesn't read stays no post. A revision that comes back with a draft and a problem carries that draft again, which the build had changed without a test asking. A finished build asks again, three times over seventeen seconds, when it can't read the issue's posts, where one failed lookup of a saved record left a finished run to be reported as stopped and built again. A saved receipt's pins are read with the modules beside its model, as the gate reads them since #829. Left as the plan has it: each use of a saved record reads and checks it again, with no memory of the last.
